clue.text: Smooth host follows woman around

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the abbreviation for a woman so it reads the other way

parts.note: Ms is the title used for a woman
a host is a great multitude, as an army is

explanation.surface: A woman is trailed everywhere by a suave entertainer at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns MS into SM, and ARMY follows it. 'host' looks like a party-giver but means a large crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone oily and ingratiating in manner.

clue.text: Celebrity takes food to the seaside

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
board is food provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A famous person brings a picnic along to the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'seaside' is read as the side of a ship at sea; starboard is the right-hand side looking forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: starboard is literally one side of a sea vessel, the right-hand one.

clue.text: Fitting quality in a head of gymnastics?

parts.note: PT, physical training, is school gymnastics
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lead gymnast shows a suitable trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland (NESS), not a leader; the PT goes between A and NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being suitable or appropriate is the quality of being apt.

clue.text: Club servant or leading ceremonial official

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
a bearer is a servant or porter

explanation.surface: Describes a member of staff at a gentlemen's club or a top ceremonial figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The macebearer walks at the head of civic processions carrying the mace, hence 'leading'.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer heads processions carrying the symbolic staff of authority.

clue.text: Notice promises about one's right to a living

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
vows are solemn promises
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A public notice of pledges concerning someone's entitlement to an income.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'living' here is a church benefice; the advowson is the right to nominate its parson.
explanation.definitionFit: In English church law this is the patron's right to present a clergyman to a benefice.

clue.text: Peculiar form of speech I caught from debate

parts.note: a dialect is a regional form of a language
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone picked up an odd way of talking from an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the art of arguing out truth through logical discussion.

clue.text: The poet of the macho video

indicators.note: of signals that the poet's name comes out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Names the poet behind a macho film.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'macho video', from the final O of macho into VID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman author of the Metamorphoses is a classical poet.

clue.text: Disturb Pooh's morning wash

indicators.note: disturb means to mess up the order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written with its S

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh is interrupted during his early wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturb' shuffles POOHS plus AM; 'morning wash' looks like one phrase but only 'wash' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair wash with soap is a shampoo.

clue.text: "Let not poor — starve" (Charles II)

parts.note: the missing word completes the dying request of King Charles II about his mistress, the actress Nell Gwyn

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Charles II reputedly said this on his deathbed of Nell Gwyn.
explanation.definitionFit: The pet form of Nell Gwyn's name completes the king's famous last words.

clue.text: Stand is uncovered for audience

indicators.note: for an audience means the words are to be heard, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to be uncovered is to be bare

explanation.surface: A stand is unveiled for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: BARE (uncovered) sounds like BEAR; 'Stand' is the verb, as in can't bear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Sign on car advertising prompt service

indicators.note: on puts the sign word after the car word in the answer

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a cue is a sign to act

explanation.surface: A sticker on a vehicle promotes a speedy repair service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prompt service' reads as quick service but means a device that prompts speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen showing a speaker's script provides prompting.

clue.text: Lady's-maid is an awful trouble

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
awful in the sense of very great, big
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A lady's servant is a terrible nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old literary term for a lady's maid, after a character in a 17th-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a dated name for a female personal attendant.

clue.text: Food complaint by one of Macaulay's citizens of Carlisle, say?

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.words: one of Macaulay's citizens of Carlisle
parts.note: Macaulay's poem The Armada says the beacon 'roused the burghers of Carlisle'

explanation.surface: A grievance voiced by one of the townsfolk in Macaulay's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: BURGHER (citizen) is said like BURGER. Carlisle is a city in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A minced meat patty is a type of food.

clue.text: Socialism's first peer is active

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the word Socialism

parts.note: to peer and to pry both mean to look nosily

explanation.surface: A socialist's leading lord is still sprightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a noble but is the verb to look closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means nimble and lively, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Sprinkle salt on chips for breakfast?

parts.note: to corn meat is to salt it, as in corned beef
chips are small flakes

explanation.surface: Asks whether to salt your chips as a morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' suggests fried potatoes, but they are small flakes; the question mark marks breakfast as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal is a typical breakfast dish.

clue.text: Sailors thank you, joining in refrain

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; ABS for more than one
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Seamen say thanks and join in the chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refrain' looks like a song's chorus but is the verb to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to hold back from doing something.

clue.text: It represents a lasting love of home

definitions.text: It represents a lasting love of home

indicators.note: represents read as re-presents, the letters set out again in a fresh order

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis scores

explanation.surface: Describes an enduring affection for one's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represents' shuffles A LASTING with O (love); the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful longing for home or the past is exactly this feeling.

clue.text: Told wife of fashionable duplex

indicators.note: fashioned anew, so these letters are made into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone reported a wife being smart about her two-storey flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges TOLD, W and OF; 'duplex' is a double-sized flat but here simply means double.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplex means having two parts, double.

clue.text: Like teaching in a cold train, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Lessons given on a chilly railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges COLD TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrinal means relating to a doctrine, a body of instruction.

clue.text: Cars constantly being hit by odd loose stones

indicators.note: loose means the letters of odd are set free to rearrange

parts.note: gems are precious stones

explanation.surface: Vehicles keep getting struck by stray rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' turns ODD into DOD, then GEMS follows. Fairground bumper cars are hit constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper cars at a funfair are bumped into all the time.

clue.text: Did without cement, so it's not so strong

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cement word goes inside

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints

explanation.surface: Building without mortar makes a weaker structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside: DID goes around LUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Watered down means weaker.

clue.text: Kind of Egyptian jar or tin with no picture on it

parts.note: a tin is a can
O is nought, zero, none
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: An Egyptian jar or a can lacking a label image.
explanation.walkthrough: Canopic jars held the organs of mummified bodies in ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopic describes the vessels used in Egyptian embalming.

clue.text: He puts out flags in the street

definitions.text: He puts out flags in the street

parts.words: He puts out flags in the street
parts.note: reads like someone decorating for a celebration, but flags are flagstones laid as paving

explanation.walkthrough: Flags are flagstones; a paviour lays paving.
explanation.definitionFit: A paviour is a workman who lays paving stones.

clue.text: Treeless plain

definitions.meaning: a ... hill or landscape is bare of trees
plain as in blunt and unadorned

explanation.definitionFit: Bare of vegetation, and also blunt or unvarnished.

clue.text: Put up fare in coach? That's fraudulent

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the coach word

parts.note: a coach is a bus

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to fare is to go or travel

explanation.surface: A coach company raised prices, which is a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns GO into OG inside BUS. 'fare' looks like a ticket price but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means sham, counterfeit.

clue.text: May I not force in this sort of bridge?

parts.note: may I not is can't I
to lever is to prise or force

explanation.surface: Someone asks permission to force their way across a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN'T I plus LEVER; apostrophes are ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: This bridge uses arms projecting from piers, supported at one end only.

clue.text: Yank accepts head of rhododendron from flower basket

indicators.note: accepts means the yank word takes the letter inside

parts.note: to yank is to tug

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the shrub

explanation.surface: An American takes a rhododendron bloom from a gardener's basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is the verb to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A trug is a shallow wooden garden basket for flowers.

clue.text: Fail to find a girl

definitions.meaning: to fail to hit or meet
a young unmarried woman, a lass

explanation.definitionFit: To fail to hit a target, and a title for a young woman.

clue.text: Newbolt got it jammed in the desert

definitions.text: Newbolt got it jammed in the desert

parts.words: Newbolt got it jammed in the desert
parts.note: Henry Newbolt's poem Vitai Lampada has a gun that jams in a desert battle as the colonel dies

explanation.walkthrough: Newbolt's line runs 'The ... 's jammed and the Colonel dead', set in the sands of the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: This early machine gun is the weapon that jams in the poem.

clue.text: Not recognised as a dark horse

definitions.meaning: a competitor of whom little is known

explanation.definitionFit: Something not identified, and a contestant with no known form.

clue.text: Takes the part of a servant of the church

definitions.text: Takes the part of a servant of the church

parts.words: Takes the part of a servant of the church
parts.note: takes the part of means sides with; a man who sides is also a church usher who takes the collection

explanation.walkthrough: SIDES (takes the part of) plus MAN (a servant) hints at the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidesman is a churchwarden's assistant who seats people and takes the collection.

clue.text: Like Test without one of the stars

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: without means the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cricket Test match minus one of its star players.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIAL loses I to give TRAL after AS. 'Test' looks like cricket but is just a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to the stars.
